newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz says no Holocaust claim proved yet.
newsitem.headline: Allianz says no Holocaust claim proved yet.

text.p: German insurance giant Allianz AG Holding said on Wednesday it had not yet identified a single valid claim against it relating to insurance policies sold to victims of Nazi persecution.

The company has launched a major campaign to help relatives of Holocaust victims track down missing assets after it was named with six other insurers in a class action suit launched earlier this year in the U.S.
The suit alleges that insurers concealed or converted the cash value and proceeds of insurance policies sold before 1946 to mainly Jewish victims of Nazi persecution.

"It would be personally unbearable if there were some sum on our books that did not belong to us, but rather to Nazi victims. As far as we know, this is not the case," Allianz Chairman Henning Schulte-Noelle told a news conference.
But, he said: "We want to be really sure about this. Therefore we will continue with our search, lawsuit or no lawsuit."
The company's 24-hour Holocaust hotline had so far not yielded a single concrete case of a valid claim against Allianz related to the Nazi period.
There had been 680 calls to the line, which was set up in mid-April, and 296 claims.
Of five claims investigated further, compensation had already been paid by the German government in three of the cases and the remaining two were still being probed.
"That is the current position, although I would of course have liked to have told you about positive solutions, or of cases that we dealt with smoothly and unbureacratically," Schulte-Noelle said.
